entries.text:
Now I'm designing the server-side Ledger service, defining a sync method and a range query method that return effects wrapping results or a LedgerFailed error, with git operations handled through the ChildProcessSpawner.

I'm working out how sync should determine the commit range by default—trying origin/HEAD, then falling back to main or master branches—then parsing `git log` output into commit records, and figuring out how to compute a stable patch-id per commit by piping `git show` output into `git patch-id`.

I also need to filter out commits already present in the agent-ledger branch, and figure out which worktrees and threads are candidates; I realize ThreadSummary doesn't currently track its worktree path, which means I'd need to fetch each thread individually or extend the summary schema to include worktree info.

For filtering I'll match threads whose worktree path equals or is nested under one of the known worktrees, plus apply a time cutoff so very old threads are skipped, falling back to the project workspace root when no explicit worktree is set.

Then for each candidate thread I'll fetch its view with labeled entries, extract commit actions, and across all threads pick a match per new commit — preferring an exact sha match, otherwise the thread with the latest matching action by start time. Finally I'll build the ledger entry by redacting outputs and filtering labels down to just the matched segment.

For writing it out, I'm setting up plumbing with a temporary index file: reading the existing agent-ledger tree if it exists, then for each entry hashing the JSON as a blob and adding it to the index under a commits path, while also merging the patch-id-to-sha mapping from the existing file. Then I write the tree and create the new commit on top of the previous one.

For updating the ref, I need to make sure git's author identity is set, falling back to a default if config is missing, then move refs/heads/agent-ledger to the new commit, and return which commits were added, skipped, or already existing.

For the range lookup, I'm iterating commits in order, trying to read each one's record from the ledger by sha, and falling back to a patch-id lookup when a direct sha match is missing.

Now I'm sketching the API surface: a repos endpoint listing candidate project roots, and a ledger endpoint that returns the computed range view, with syncing handled only via CLI rather than the UI.

For the CLI side, I need to avoid a filename clash with the existing ledger service file on case-insensitive filesystems, so I'll call it ledgerCli.ts with sync and show subcommands exposed through a run script. But I'm realizing there's a startup timing issue: since codex session listing loads in the background on app start, running sync immediately could miss codex threads that haven't finished loading yet, so I need to account for that race condition.

To fix the race, I'll add a `ready` effect to CodexSessions that resolves once the first background refresh completes, using a Deferred that gets fulfilled on either success or failure, and have the ledger await that before listing. Now I'll move on to writing the Ledger service itself, starting with the ThreadSummary.worktree domain change first.



Now I'll work on the server side Ledger service, which syncs entries to the agent-ledger branch and reads commit ranges. First I need two prerequisite changes: adding working directory to thread summaries so the ledger can filter sessions by repo, and adding a way to wait for Codex's initial background listing so early syncs don't miss its sessions.

Now I'm setting up tests for the Ledger service using a real git repo in a temp directory, with a stubbed ThreadStore containing a thread whose worktree points to that repo and entries for commit actions.

I need to flesh out the flow: initializing the repo, making commits on main and a feature branch, then syncing and verifying the ledger branch contains commit JSON files, that the working tree stays untouched, that range queries return matching entries, and that amended commits still resolve via patch-id matching, plus checking that a second sync is idempotent. I'll control commit timestamps with GIT_COMMITTER_DATE so they align with the thread action times used in assertions.

entries.text: The CLI is working, so I'll commit step 2 now with the time-match path using -q. I'm thinking it's better to run a real sync early against the actual repo to validate it writes the ledger branch correctly, rather than waiting until all commits exist, since sync is incremental anyway.

feat(ledger): sync agent commits onto the agent-ledger branch

Ledger service + `vp run ledger -- sync|show` CLI. Sync finds the sessions
that worked in the repo (or its git worktrees), ties each commit in the
range to the `git commit` action that made it, and writes the redacted
history since the previous commit as commits/<sha>.json on agent-ledger.
It writes through a private index (hash-object / update-index / commit-tree
/ update-ref), so the working tree and HEAD are never touched. Reading a
range falls back to patch-id when a commit was rebased or amended.

Thread summaries now carry their working directory, and the Codex source
exposes `ready` so syncs don't miss sessions still being listed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
